examples.ko: 영속적 관계를 바라지만 현실은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: I want a lasting relationship, but reality isn't easy.
This system probably won't last forever.
That company dreams of growing continuously.
I think nothing in the world is permanent.
For the effect to last, you have to keep making an effort.
A tattoo is permanent, so it is hard to remove.

explain: '영구적'과 비슷하지만 '영속적'은 끊어지지 않고 계속 이어진다는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '영속적인', '영속적으로'처럼 쓰고, 반대말은 '일시적'이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '영구적' (permanent), but '영속적' stresses that something continues without breaking. It is usually used as '영속적인' or '영속적으로', and the opposite is '일시적' (temporary).

en: being first in line for something

examples.en: For me, family always comes first, above everything.

examples.ko: 이번 이사에서 영순위 조건은 역과 가까운 곳이에요.
examples.en: My top condition for this move is a place close to the station.
They say if you pass, you get first priority for a dorm room.

examples.ko: 제가 갖고 싶은 영순위 선물은 새 운동화예요.
examples.en: The gift I want most is a new pair of sneakers.
Right now, health has to be the top priority.

examples.ko: 이번 시상식에서도 그 가수가 영순위라는 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say that singer is the top favorite at this awards show too.

explain: '1순위'나 '최우선'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는데, 0이 1보다 앞선다는 느낌 때문에 '무엇보다 먼저'를 강조할 때 많이 써요. 사람을 '영순위 후보'처럼 가장 유력한 대상으로 가리킬 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '1순위' or '최우선', but because 0 comes before 1, it adds the feel of 'before anything else'. It can also point to a person as the most likely candidate, as in '영순위 후보'.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나이는 어려도 정말 영악해요.
examples.en: That child is really shrewd even though he's young.
Be careful not to be fooled by a crafty merchant.

examples.ko: 동생이 영악하게 부모님께 용돈을 받아 냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling cleverly got pocket money out of our parents.
That friend is shrewd, but has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 영악해서 손해 보는 일은 절대 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so shrewd that he never does anything that costs him.

examples.ko: 영악했던 그 후배는 결국 먼저 승진했어요.
examples.en: That shrewd junior colleague ended up getting promoted first.

explain: 똑똑하다는 뜻이지만 '영악하다'는 자기에게 이익이 되게 꾀를 잘 쓴다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬만으로 들리지 않을 때가 많아요. 순수하게 머리가 좋다고 칭찬할 때는 '영특하다'나 '똑똑하다'가 더 알맞아요.
explain_en: It means smart, but '영악하다' suggests using tricks to benefit oneself, so it often doesn't sound like pure praise. To simply praise someone's brains, '영특하다' or '똑똑하다' fits better.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 들려주시는 영웅담은 언제 들어도 재미있어요.
examples.en: Grandfather's hero stories are fun no matter when I hear them.
The children's eyes sparkled as they listened to the hero story.

examples.ko: 모임에서 자기 영웅담만 늘어놓는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone at the gathering who only keeps going on about his own heroic tales.
They say this hero story is passed down in many countries.

examples.ko: 그 책은 평범한 사람들의 영웅담을 모았어요.
examples.en: That book collects hero stories of ordinary people.
I want to become brave like the protagonist of a hero story.

explain: 영웅의 이야기를 뜻하지만, 일상에서는 자기가 한 대단한 일을 자랑하듯 말하는 이야기에도 '영웅담을 늘어놓다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '무용담'이 있는데, 용감하게 싸우거나 모험한 이야기에 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Besides stories about heroes, it is used in daily talk for someone boasting about great things they did, as in '영웅담을 늘어놓다'. A similar word is '무용담', which fits stories of brave fights or adventures better.

examples.ko: 영웅심에 위험한 일에 뛰어들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't jump into dangerous things out of a hero complex.
That friend has too strong a desire to be a hero.

examples.ko: 영웅심 때문에 혼자 일을 다 맡았어요.
examples.en: Because of my hero complex, I took on all the work alone.
It was an act that came from a small streak of wanting to be a hero.
The child tried to help his friend out of a wish to be a hero.

examples.ko: 괜한 영웅심을 부리다가 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: You could get hurt showing off an unnecessary hero act.

explain: 남 앞에서 멋지게 나서고 싶은 마음을 말해요. '영웅심을 부리다', '영웅심에 ~하다'처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 조금 무모하다는 느낌이 들어갈 때가 많아요. '영웅심리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the urge to step forward and look impressive in front of others. It is often used as '영웅심을 부리다' or '영웅심에 ~하다', frequently with a hint of recklessness. People also say '영웅심리'.

examples.en: We humans also belong to the primates, scientifically speaking.
Chimpanzees are the primates closest to humans.
Primates are good at grasping things with their hands.

examples.ko: 동물원에서 아이와 함께 영장류 우리를 구경했어요.
examples.en: At the zoo, I looked at the primate enclosure with my child.
This institute studies the behavior of primates.
Gorillas and monkeys are also classified as primates.

explain: 원숭이, 침팬지, 고릴라, 사람을 한데 묶는 분류 이름이에요. 일상에서는 '원숭이'라고 말하고, '영장류'는 과학 수업이나 뉴스, 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is the group name that covers monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and humans. In daily talk people say '원숭이', while '영장류' appears mostly in science classes, the news and explanatory writing.

examples.en: Heave-ho, let's lift this box together!
Heave-ho! Just a little more effort.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들면서 영차 하고 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: I made a 'heave-ho' sound as I lifted the heavy load.
Heave-ho, I finally made it all the way to the top of the mountain!

examples.ko: 아이가 의자 위로 영차 하고 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The child climbed up onto the chair with a 'heave-ho'.

examples.ko: 다 같이 영차 하고 줄을 당겨요.
examples.en: Everyone say 'heave-ho' together and pull the rope.

explain: 무거운 것을 들거나 힘을 모을 때 내는 소리예요. 여럿이 박자를 맞출 때는 '영차영차'나 '어영차'처럼 이어서 말하기도 해요. 귀엽거나 장난스러운 느낌도 있어서 아이들이 힘쓰는 장면에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the sound people make when lifting something heavy or putting their strength together. When several people keep time, they may repeat it as '영차영차' or say '어영차'. It also sounds cute and playful, so it often appears in scenes of children straining.

examples.en: That child has been really bright since he was little.
My bright nephew can already read Hangul.
My puppy is smart, so training goes quickly.

examples.ko: 영특하기로 소문난 학생이 우리 반에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a student in our class famous for being exceptionally bright.

examples.ko: 영특하게 생긴 아이가 큰 소리로 인사했어요.
examples.en: A bright-looking child greeted me in a loud voice.

examples.ko: 영특하다는 칭찬을 어릴 때부터 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: I have often heard praise for being bright since I was young.

explain: 주로 어른이 아이나 동물의 총명함을 칭찬할 때 써요. 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 하는 칭찬 같은 느낌이라서, 윗사람에게나 자기 자신에게 쓰면 어색해요.
explain_en: Adults mostly use it to praise the brightness of a child or an animal. It feels like praise from a senior to a junior, so it sounds odd when used toward someone older or about yourself.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 권력에 영합한다는 비판을 받아요.
examples.en: That politician is criticized for currying favor with power.
I speak honestly without sucking up to my boss.

examples.ko: 인기에 영합해서 만든 영화는 금방 잊혀요.
examples.en: Movies made just to chase popularity are quickly forgotten.

examples.ko: 남의 비위에 영합하며 사는 건 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate living by pandering to other people's moods.

examples.ko: 여론에 영합한 정책은 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: Policies that pander to public opinion don't last long.

examples.ko: 대중에게 영합하는 노래만 만들고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to make only songs that pander to the masses.

explain: 자기 생각 없이 윗사람이나 대중의 비위를 맞춘다는 부정적인 뜻이에요. '권력에, 여론에, 인기에'처럼 '에/에게'와 같이 쓰고, 뉴스나 글에 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '아부하다', '비위를 맞추다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It has a negative sense of pleasing superiors or the public without a view of your own. It is used with '에/에게', as in '권력에, 여론에, 인기에', and appears mostly in news and writing. In everyday talk people more often say '아부하다' or '비위를 맞추다'.

examples.ko: 어선이 우리 영해를 침범했다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a fishing boat had intruded into our territorial waters.
Territorial waters usually extend up to 12 nautical miles from the coast.

examples.ko: 외국 배가 영해에 들어오면 해경이 확인해요.
examples.en: When a foreign ship enters the territorial waters, the coast guard checks it.

examples.ko: 배가 영해 밖으로 나가면 공해라고 해요.
examples.en: When a ship goes outside the territorial waters, it's called the high seas.
The coast guard patrols the territorial waters all night.
I marked the boundary of the territorial waters on the map.

explain: 한 나라의 바다 영역을 말하고, 땅인 '영토', 하늘인 '영공'과 함께 묶어서 자주 말해요. 영해 밖의 바다는 '공해'라고 해요. 주로 뉴스나 사회 수업에서 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a country's sea area, and is often mentioned together with '영토' (land) and '영공' (airspace). The sea beyond it is called '공해' (high seas). You mostly meet it in the news and social studies classes.

examples.ko: 절에서 템플스테이를 하며 새벽 예불에 참여했어요.
examples.en: During a temple stay, I took part in the dawn service.
The monks hold a Buddhist service every morning.
When it was time for the service, a bell rang.

examples.ko: 저녁 예불이 끝나고 다 같이 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: After the evening service ended, we all had tea together.

examples.ko: 처음 해 본 예불은 생각보다 길었어요.
examples.en: The service I tried for the first time was longer than I expected.
Many monks start their day with the service.

explain: 절에서 부처님께 절하고 경을 외며 드리는 의식이에요. '예불을 드리다'처럼 말하고, 템플스테이에서는 보통 새벽과 저녁에 체험해요.
explain_en: It is the ritual of bowing and chanting before the Buddha at a temple. People say '예불을 드리다', and at a temple stay you can usually experience it at dawn and in the evening.

en: lightly; as if it were nothing special

examples.en: Don't take those words lightly.
My friend lies as if it were nothing, and I'm worried.
I don't let even a small mistake pass as no big deal.

examples.ko: 예사로 지나쳤던 일이 나중에 큰 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: Something I had brushed off became a big problem later.

examples.ko: 그는 약속을 어기는 걸 예사로 여겨요.
examples.en: He treats breaking promises as an ordinary thing.

examples.ko: 이 증상은 예사로 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat this symptom as nothing.

explain: '대수롭지 않게, 보통 일처럼'이라는 느낌으로 '예사로 넘기다, 예사로 보다, 예사로 여기다, 예사로 하다'처럼 뒤의 동사와 함께 써요. '예사롭지 않다'가 훨씬 자주 나오는 형태라서 같이 익혀 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of 'as if it were nothing special' and goes with verbs such as '예사로 넘기다, 예사로 보다, 예사로 여기다, 예사로 하다'. The negative form '예사롭지 않다' is much more common, so it is worth learning together.

examples.ko: 이 동네에서는 정전이 예삿일이라 다들 놀라지 않아요.
examples.en: In this neighborhood power cuts are routine, so nobody is surprised.
Being late is a routine thing for that friend.

examples.ko: 밤에 들리는 그 소리는 예삿일이 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: That sound at night seems to be no ordinary matter.
Working overtime has become like an ordinary thing on our team.

examples.ko: 이런 일을 예삿일로 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat a matter like this as ordinary.

examples.ko: 예삿일은 아니니까 빨리 병원에 가 봐요.
examples.en: This isn't something minor, so go to the hospital quickly.

explain: '예삿일이 아니다'라는 형태로 '심상치 않다, 가볍게 볼 일이 아니다'라는 뜻을 나타낼 때가 가장 많아요. 사이시옷이 들어가서 [예산닐]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It is most often used in the form '예삿일이 아니다', meaning 'this is serious, not something to take lightly'. It has a sai-siot, so it is pronounced [예산닐].

en: be subject to; be subordinate to

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랫동안 이웃 나라에 예속돼 있었어요.
examples.en: That country was subordinate to a neighboring country for a long time.
I felt tied down to the company, so I quit.
I want to live without being enslaved by money.

examples.ko: 예속되어 지내던 사람들이 마침내 자유를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The people who had lived in subjugation finally gained freedom.

examples.ko: 이 단체는 어느 정당에도 예속될 수 없어요.
examples.en: This organization cannot be subordinate to any political party.
I want to change a life enslaved to my smartphone.

explain: 힘이 센 쪽에 매여 자유롭지 못한 상태를 말하고, 보통 '~에 예속되다'로 써요. 정치·경제·역사 글에 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '매이다', '얽매이다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes being bound to a stronger party without freedom, and is normally used as '~에 예속되다'. It appears a lot in political, economic and historical writing, while in daily talk '매이다' or '얽매이다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I got through the audition's preliminary screening safely.
Last year I failed the preliminary round, which was a real shame.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 아홉 시에 예심이 열려요.
examples.en: The preliminary screening takes place tomorrow at nine in the morning.
The participants in the preliminary round get number tags and wait.

examples.ko: 이번 예심에는 천 명이 넘게 지원했어요.
examples.en: Over a thousand people applied for this preliminary screening.
The preliminary screening of this contest is held privately.

explain: 본선에 올라갈 사람을 먼저 가려내는 심사예요. '예선'은 경기에서 많이 쓰고, '예심'은 오디션이나 공모전처럼 심사로 가리는 곳에서 자주 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본선'이에요.
explain_en: It is the first screening that picks who goes on to the main round. '예선' is common for sports matches, while '예심' is often used for judged events such as auditions and contests. Its counterpart is '본선' (the main round).

examples.en: This is the planned site where a new park will be built.
Residents near the planned factory site are opposing it.
Land prices went up in the area announced as the planned site.
I went and saw the planned new-town site in person.

examples.ko: 공사 예정지 앞에 안내판이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A notice board stands in front of the planned construction site.

examples.ko: 새 집 이사 예정지가 회사에서 너무 멀어요.
examples.en: The place we plan to move to is too far from my office.

explain: '건설 예정지, 개발 예정지, 이주 예정지'처럼 앞말과 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. '후보지'는 아직 고르는 중인 곳이고, '예정지'는 그곳으로 하기로 이미 정해진 곳을 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually combined with a preceding word, as in '건설 예정지', '개발 예정지' or '이주 예정지'. A '후보지' is a candidate still being chosen, while an '예정지' is a place already decided on.

examples.ko: 서비스에 가입하려면 예치금을 먼저 내야 해요.
examples.en: To sign up for the service, you have to pay the deposit first.
You get the deposit back when you finish using it.

examples.ko: 이 서비스를 쓰려면 예치금이 얼마나 필요해요?
examples.en: How much deposit do I need to use this service?
You have to transfer the deposit as well.

examples.ko: 예치금 없이 빌릴 수 있는 곳을 찾아요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a place where I can borrow without a deposit.

examples.ko: 렌터카를 빌릴 때 예치금으로 20만 원을 맡겼어요.
examples.en: When I rented a car, I left 200,000 won as a deposit.

explain: 나중에 돌려받는다는 점에서 '보증금'과 비슷하지만, 집을 빌릴 때는 보통 '보증금'이라고 말해요. '예치금'은 서비스나 계좌에 미리 맡겨 두는 돈을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '보증금' in that you get it back later, but when renting a home people normally say '보증금'. '예치금' is used for money placed in advance with a service or an account.

examples.en: I deposit my stocks in a brokerage account.
It's safe if you deposit your money in a bank.

examples.ko: 고객이 맡긴 자금은 따로 예탁해야 해요.
examples.en: Funds that customers entrust must be deposited separately.

examples.ko: 그는 보유한 주식을 모두 증권사에 예탁했어요.
examples.en: He deposited all the stocks he held with the brokerage.

examples.ko: 증권사에 예탁한 주식은 쉽게 거래할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Stocks deposited with a brokerage can be traded easily.
It is a system where the deposit is placed with a bank.

explain: 돈이나 주식을 금융 기관에 맡긴다는 뜻의 금융 용어예요. '예치하다'와 비슷하게 쓰이고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '맡기다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a financial term for placing money or stocks with a financial institution. It is used much like '예치하다', and in everyday talk people simply say '맡기다'.

examples.en: If parents spoil a child too much, the child becomes ill-mannered.
Grandmother raises her grandchild by indulging him.
I decided not to raise my child by spoiling him.
He grew up in an indulgent atmosphere, so he has no patience.
Please don't keep indulging him just because he's the youngest.
I regret having spoiled him so much.

explain: 아이가 원하는 것을 다 들어주고 받아 주는 것을 말하고, 버릇없게 만든다는 부정적인 느낌이 들어 있어요. '아이를 오냐오냐하다'나 '오냐오냐 키우다'처럼 주로 아이에게 써요.
explain_en: It means giving in to everything a child wants, and it carries a negative sense of making the child ill-mannered. It is mostly used for children, as in '아이를 오냐오냐하다' or '오냐오냐 키우다'.

en: May and June; May or June

examples.ko: 오뉴월 한낮에는 밖에 오래 못 있어요.
examples.en: At midday in early summer, I can't stay outside for long.
This year the rainy season has already started from early summer.

examples.ko: 오뉴월에는 해가 길어서 저녁 늦게까지 밝아요.
examples.en: In early summer the days are long, so it stays light until late evening.
The sunshine of early summer is much stronger than you'd think.

examples.ko: 오뉴월 땡볕 아래서 일하던 할머니가 생각나요.
examples.en: I think of my grandmother working under the scorching early-summer sun.
In the heat of early summer, you lose your appetite too.

explain: 원래 음력 오월과 유월을 합친 말이라 요즘 달력의 5~6월과 꼭 같지는 않지만, 초여름의 더위나 햇볕을 말할 때 '오뉴월 더위', '오뉴월 땡볕'처럼 많이 써요. 속담에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 오뉴월 감기는 개도 안 걸린다는데 저는 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: They say even a dog doesn't catch a cold in early summer, but I did.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 감기에 걸린 사람을 조심성이 없거나 몸이 약하다고 놀릴 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used to tease someone who catches a cold in summer, implying carelessness or weakness.
phrases.en_equiv: only the careless catch a summer cold

explain_en: It originally combines the fifth and sixth months of the lunar calendar, so it doesn't exactly match May and June on today's calendar, but it is commonly used for early-summer heat and sunshine, as in '오뉴월 더위' and '오뉴월 땡볕'. It also appears often in proverbs.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks are so plump and adorable.
He gripped the toy tightly with his chubby hand.
The puppy has put on weight and become plump.
I ate dumplings with plump shrimp inside.
My younger sibling had a chubby face as a child.
Being called chubby sounds like praise for being cute.

explain: '통통하다'와 비슷하지만 작고 귀엽게 살이 올라 있는 느낌이 더 강해요. 아기의 볼, 작은 손, 강아지처럼 귀여운 대상에 잘 어울려요. 몸집이 큰 어른에게는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '통통하다' but has a stronger feel of being small and cutely plump. It suits cute things like a baby's cheeks, small hands or puppies, and is not usually used for large adults.
